name: XPRS
aliases: eXtended Postgres on Raid and Sprite
tagline: 1988 Berkeley research DBMS: POSTGRES on RAID disks and the Sprite OS for parallel, highly available queries.
description: XPRS (eXtended Postgres on Raid and Sprite) was a late-1980s UC Berkeley project led by Michael Stonebraker, Randy Katz, David Patterson and John Ousterhout. It set out to show that a general-purpose DBMS on a general-purpose operating system and a shared-memory multiprocessor could match specialised systems in transaction processing, complex ad-hoc queries and large objects at once. The design combined a modified POSTGRES, the Sprite network OS and RAID disk arrays, with a fast-path interface, special concurrency control, a two-dimensional file system and intra-query parallelism. Its parallel query optimisation work, notably by Wei Hong, and its pairing with RAID made it influential, though it never became a product.
statusNote: Late-1980s research prototype at UC Berkeley; never released as a product. Ideas carried into parallel query optimisation and POSTGRES lineage.

pricing.notes: Never sold or distributed as a product.

scale.notes: Targeted shared-memory multiprocessors such as the Sequent Symmetry with RAID storage.

strengths: Early demonstration of intra-query parallelism on shared-memory multiprocessors
Co-designed DBMS, operating system and RAID storage in one research effort
Influential work on two-phase parallel query optimisation
weaknesses: Research prototype only; no code or product available
Tied to 1980s hardware and the Sprite OS
useCases: Studying the history of parallel database systems
Background reading for query parallelism courses
